findings.summary: I read all of review-service, review-journal, migration 014, review-client, review-page, the loop-auth host diff, both new test files, REPORT.md, REVIEW_LOCAL_SLICE.md and the approved SYNTHETIC_REVIEW_LIFECYCLE_SLICE. Most of the slice matches the card: the seven checks are server-checked and missing ones are reported by name; snapshots are pinned to the locked generation head, job and revision; snapshots and withdrawals cannot be changed afterwards and only one snapshot is allowed per revision; the journal has its own keys and namespace and refuses wrong or replaced stores; the HTTP route checks are strict; and the tests use the real fixture objects. But one fenced pending command blocks the whole household's review permanently, a test asserts that outcome as the expected result, and the UI cannot recover from a stale-digest conflict. My reading of the mandatory originals was also incomplete (PROJECT_CONTEXT v1.98 through EOF, the product files, the four engineering-v1 files, 00-B CONTRACTS, the 00-C map, the generation report and setup r1/r2 were not read in full), so this review could not support PASS in any case.

findings.title: One fenced pending command blocks review for the whole household forever
findings.problem: If authority changes after the primary commit but before the ACK, the command stays unacknowledged forever. Cases: a generation edit or regeneration during the append (the test at tests/loop-review-service.test.mjs:45 does exactly this), a generation journal-pending state when finish() calls source(), a consent withdrawal followed by re-consent, or a founder demotion. Reconcile can never succeed: verifyRow (line 295) requires the row's old pin to equal the current pin, and ownRow (line 289) requires the same epoch and actor. Meanwhile pending() (line 273) returns review_pending for any unacknowledged row anywhere in the household, and command() (line 379) refuses every new write in the household with journal_unavailable. So after an ordinary concurrent draft edit, every request in that household loses its private view and can never be reviewed again; other requests show 'pending' with no recovery reference. The card requires that withdrawal and authority rechecks fence old pending work and that only dependent writes are blocked. A permanent household-wide deadlock is not meaningful failure handling. The test at line 45 asserts review_pending as the final state and never checks any way forward.
findings.fix_check: Choose and document a resolution for pending commands that can no longer be acknowledged: for example a terminal fenced/no-effect state that does not count toward projection, readiness or snapshots, or recognising rows whose pin, epoch or actor can no longer become current. It must not change history or acknowledge stale evidence. Extend the source-change-during-append and append-time-withdrawal-then-reconsent tests: after the fence, a fresh review on the new source succeeds, other requests in the household stay readable, and no stale review, snapshot or ACK appears.

findings.title: Stale-digest/CAS conflict leaves the UI stuck, then wrongly blames authority
findings.problem: A 409 from command() (for example when the source changes between a poll and the click) keeps the intent with rejected=false. The only controls offered are Retry, which returns 409 again, and Reconcile. For a command that was never committed, reconcile() returns 403, because ownRow(undefined) fails as 'denied' (review-service.mjs:416). The UI then runs denied() and shows 'Founder or test authority changed', clearing the selection. The card requires that a stale digest gives an actionable failure. Here there is no truthful dismiss path and the message is wrong. Stale-digest behaviour is only tested by raw HTTP posts; no UI test sends a stale-digest command through the page.
findings.fix_check: Reconcile of an unknown command ID, same actor and scope, returns a distinct response with no private data instead of 403. The UI then offers an explicit dismiss and reread for a command confirmed absent, while keeping the original key when the outcome is genuinely ambiguous. Add a JSDOM test that edits the source between render and click and checks the actionable message, that selection and authority are not wrongly cleared, and that a fresh review can be recorded afterwards.

findings.title: REPORT blob table and doc/report status text are stale
findings.problem: The REPORT table lists server/review-service.mjs as blob 024dcc5f…, but the reviewed pin is 6fd3ddb2…. REPORT and docs/loop/REVIEW_LOCAL_SLICE.md still describe themselves as a 'response-only source candidate' with 'authored assertions, not passing results'. The review-page.mjs header (lines 4-6) still mentions an 'unchanged stage1 service' and says 'No tests or browser verification are claimed'. These conflict with the evidence that source pins are bound to exact blobs.
findings.fix_check: The REPORT blob table matches the final pinned blobs. The doc, report and page-header status text say which evidence was actually executed and which is still outstanding.

findings.title: Mandatory original reading not completed in this review
findings.problem: Mandatory originals not read in full in this review: PROJECT_CONTEXT v1.98 (1,342 lines), SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, AGENTS, GOVERNANCE, PRODUCT_V1/PRODUCT_DECISIONS, the four engineering-v1 files, 00-B CONTRACTS, the 00-C map, the 05-B card, the generation contract/report/carried findings, the 04-C acceptance notes and setup r1/r2. The APPROVAL-010 entry could not be displayed because its line is too long. Read in full: the approved slice spec, all ten app files in scope and the host diff. The card says incomplete mandatory reading cannot support PASS.
findings.fix_check: The next feature round (or a small incremental final review) reads every mandatory original through EOF and states complete coverage before any PASS.

findings.title: Two corrections may name the same predecessor (branching lineage)
findings.problem: A correction may name any earlier snapshot from a different revision, including one already withdrawn or already corrected. Lineage can therefore branch rather than form a single chain. The card does not forbid this, but it is not documented.
findings.fix_check: Either document that branching is intended, or restrict predecessors to the latest non-superseded snapshot and add a test.
